He also pursued competitive and multihull sailing.

long_biography.plain_text:
At 20, François Bich began as a production agent in BIC's Paris factory. When his father, Marcel, bought lighter maker Flaminaire, he sent François to Redon to lead the new activity. Bich simplified the mechanism, tightened control over each production step and helped launch the first BIC disposable lighter two years later.

He remained responsible for the lighter category for more than four decades, turning it into one of the group's signature businesses. Alongside that operating work, he spent 42 years on BIC's board and 28 years as executive vice-president. He also held shares directly and through family holding Société M.B.D., whose supervisory board he chaired. He retired from executive duties in 2016 and died in 2026, aged 76.
